property_summary: The reference function always executes exactly tos.length iterations (never an out-of-bounds access on tos), while the buggy version may index out of bounds in tos when tos.length < vs.length, causing either a revert or a discrepancy in the number of successful external calls.

For any valid input, the reference C always returns true without reverting; the buggy version can revert due to an out-of-bounds array access when vs.length differs from tos.length (despite the earlier equality check).

The reference always completes without reverting and returns true for any input where tos.length equals vs.length, while the buggy version reverts whenever vs.length differs from tos.length (due to the equality check removal) instead of reverting from the equality check.

For any input where the arrays are equal length, both versions iterate the same number of times, but the buggy version uses vs.length as the loop bound and will index out of bounds on tos when vs.length > tos.length, causing a revert instead of returning true.

For any input where tos.length equals vs.length, the reference always completes the full number of external calls equal to tos.length, while the buggy version may iterate beyond tos bounds when vs.length differs, causing a revert that prevents the same number of successful calls.
A call to transfer with contract_address == address(c) must always revert in the reference, but succeeds in the mutant, so the presence of a revert distinguishes them.

For any call to transfer with contract_address equal to the contract itself, the reference always reverts due to the validAddress modifier, while the mutant allows the call to proceed, causing a change in the return value or state.
For any call to transfer where contract_address equals address(c), the reference always reverts, but the mutant proceeds without revert.
For any call to transfer where contract_address equals address(c), the correct contract always reverts, while the mutant proceeds without revert.
